title: Microwave-to-optical transduction using magnon–exciton coupling
task: Realize coherent microwave-to-optical transduction via magnon-exciton coupling in antiferromagnet
key_results: Coherent conversion over 300-MHz broadband window in CrSBr using AFM resonance modulation; multiple exciton-polariton resonances inherit magnon response without cavity enhancement
comments: Novel hybrid magnon-exciton platform with potential for higher cooperativity via reduced magnetic volume and cavities, though low conversion efficiency and thermal magnon damping may limit practical quantum network integration.

model_io.model: Layered antiferromagnet CrSBr with exciton-magnon coupling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Strong exciton-magnon coupling enables efficient resonant light-matter modulation for broadband microwave-optical transduction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; coherent conversion across 300-MHz window without cavity enhancement

title: Single-gate, multipartite entanglement on a room-temperature quantum register
task: Demonstrate parallel multipartite entangling gates on room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy centers
key_results: Four-qubit GHZ state generated in 14.8 μs with 0.92(4) fidelity—10× faster than sequential gates; four-qubit sequential gate fidelity only 0.69(3)
comments: Significant fidelity improvement and speedup via parallelization, establishing foundation for scalable entanglement generation, though crosstalk and decoherence in larger arrays remain concerns.

model_io.model: Nitrogen-vacancy center electron + nuclear spin system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parallel multi-qubit gates avoid sequential crosstalk and approach fundamental hyperfine coupling speed limits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; four-qubit fidelity 92% vs 69% for sequential approach

title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
task: Demonstrate on-chip all-optical magnetization switching in integrated photonics
key_results: 90% switching contrast achieved in 500-nm Co/Gd Hall crosses using femtosecond pulses in silicon nitride waveguides; stochastic switching in larger devices due to non-uniform absorption
comments: Critical demonstration of integrated photonic-spintronic control, though device scaling requirements for robust switching limit immediate applicability.

model_io.model: Silicon nitride waveguide with Co/Gd Hall cross on-chip

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-uniform optical absorption causes domain-wall relaxation and thermally-assisted (de)pinning in large devices
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via finite-element simulations; explains switching contrast reduction

title: Generation of a high-intensity, superthermal muonium beam for gravity and laser spectroscopy experiments
task: Generate high-brightness muonium beam for gravity and spectroscopy tests
key_results: Superthermal muonium beam extracted from superfluid helium with yields matching highest diffuse sources; enables per-cent-level gravitational acceleration measurement
comments: Breakthrough for testing gravity with second-generation fermions, though muon lifetime constraints require rapid downstream experiments.

model_io.model: Superfluid helium muonium extraction system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Superfluid helium enables efficient muonium thermalization and extraction with narrow velocity spread
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; superthermal beam generated with sufficient brightness for interferometry

title: An algorithm to generate two-dimensional critical lattice models using competing anyon condensation
task: Generate 2D critical lattice models from 3D topological order boundaries
key_results: Algorithm generates infinite family of critical lattice models including previously unknown CFTs; recovers Haagerup symmetry theories and identifies three candidate new theories
comments: Elegant connection between string-net models and CFT classification, though experimental realization remains challenging.

model_io.model: String-net model with engineered boundary conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Commensurate non-commuting anyon condensation induces CFT critical points in 2D lattice boundaries
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; algebraic data precisely encodes critical couplings

title: Electrification mechanisms in sliding liquid and frozen drops
task: Elucidate charge transfer mechanisms in sliding polar and non-polar liquids and frozen drops
key_results: Frozen non-polar compounds exhibit charging similar to liquid phase despite reduced ion mobility; frozen polar compounds accumulate substantial charge despite minimal ions; indicates dual ion- and electron-transfer mechanisms
comments: Important evidence for electron-transfer contribution to tribochemistry, challenging ion-transfer-only models, though temperature-dependent phase transitions complicate mechanistic interpretation.

model_io.model: Water drop or self-ionizing liquid sliding on insulating surface

hypotheses.hypothesis: Slide electrification operates via dual mechanisms: ion transfer (polar) and electron transfer (temperature/electronegativity dependent)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; non-polar liquid behavior invariant across phases indicates electron-dominated pathway
